article.title: About SaxonC
article.p: SaxonC is a version of Saxon developed by cross-compiling the Java source code to executables that run on the C/C++ platform, with extensions for PHP and Python. All features of Saxon have been ported, other than those (such as collations) that are necessarily platform dependent. In particular, SaxonC provides processing in XSLT, XQuery and XPath, and Schema validation. It therefore makes these processing capabilities available to a plethora of other languages that are strongly coupled to C/C++ such as PHP, Perl, Python, and Ruby. (For instance, saxon-node uses SaxonC to create an interface with Node.js.)

SaxonC 11 is built from the SaxonJ 11 Java product using Excelsior JET Enterprise 15.3 edition (MP1). The APIs support the current W3C Recommendations: XSLT 3.0, XQuery 3.1, XPath 3.1 and Schema Validation 1.0/1.1. See the main Saxon 11 documentation Standards Conformance section for full details.

SaxonC is released in three separate editions, as on the Java and .NET platforms: the commercial products Enterprise Edition (SaxonC-EE) and Professional Edition (SaxonC-PE), and the opensource product Home Edition (SaxonC-HE). See the feature matrix to compare the features of the HE, PE and EE products.
Versions are available for the following platforms: Linux 64-bit, Mac OS and Windows 64-bit. (Note that from SaxonC 1.2 versions are no longer available for 32-bit systems.)
